title: Harborview Pension Fund: Contoso Equity Fund Class C fees (live Teams demo call)
shows: Share-class precision: Class C is the product and Class A was only a comparison; two seller tasks with resolved dates.
notes: Two voices, played into ONE microphone, so Teams attributes every line to the host. Design rules: every commitment is the seller's (a customer commitment would be filed as a seller task), no 'today', 'tonight' or 'tomorrow' (call dates are UTC, so they drift near midnight), and the share class is corrected out loud (Class A is rejected, Class C is the product).

gold.notes: Class A is named only to be rejected, so it is not a gold product. 'By Monday' and 'by Wednesday' on a Friday call resolve to 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-11.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Hi Dana, it's Aisha from Contoso Woodgrove. Can you hear me okay?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Hi Aisha, yes, loud and clear. Thanks for making the time.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Of course. How's the week treating you? I know it's been a busy stretch with the quarter-end reviews.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Busy is an understatement. Committee season never really ends, but we're getting there.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I hear you. So, last time we spoke, you mentioned Harborview was pulling together a large-cap core mandate. I had the Class A shares of the Contoso Equity Fund in my notes. Is that still the one you're looking at?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Not quite. It's not the Class A shares. We're looking at the Contoso Equity Fund, Class C, because that's the only one our custodian's platform lists.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Thanks for the catch, Dana. So that's Class C, which means no front-end sales charge, but there's an ongoing distribution fee and a deferred sales charge if you redeem in the first year.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Right. What's the total expense ratio on Class C, and how does it stack up against what we'd pay on Class A?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Class C runs about one point six percent all in, and Class A is closer to ninety-five basis points before any sales charge. On a position your size, that gap matters, so the breakpoints are worth a look as well.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's helpful. Could you put the numbers in writing, class by class? Our investment committee will want to see them before they approve anything.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Absolutely. I'll send you the fee comparison by Monday, with the expense ratios and the sales charge schedule side by side.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Thanks. The other thing is that the one-pager in our file is from last quarter, so I'm not sure the holdings and expense figures are current.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Good catch. Let me get the updated fact sheet over to you by Wednesday.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Perfect. Our committee meets on the twentieth, so having both documents before then would be ideal.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Understood. And if the committee ever wants a lower-cost share class down the road, a conversion is straightforward once you're past the breakpoints.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Good to know. Is there a due diligence questionnaire we should expect to fill out on our side?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Not for a fund your platform already lists, though your committee may have its own checklist. Dana, you would know better than I would.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: We do have a short internal form, but my team handles that, so there's nothing for you to complete.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Perfect, that keeps it simple. Anything else on your mind before we wrap up?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No, I think that covers it. Thanks, Aisha.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Thank you, Dana. Enjoy the rest of your week.
